judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Three Performance Objectives (same coordinate rank 2). The first (Money topic, Mensuration and Geometry theme) asks pupils to shop with money ≤₦20 using the idea of addition and subtraction; the second (Subtraction topic, Basic Operations theme) asks pupils to mention the need for correct subtraction of numbers and fractions in everyday activities. They sit under different themes/topics, but share substantive conceptual coherence: both connect subtraction to real-world/everyday use, one applying it in shopping and the other articulating its everyday necessity. This is meaningful reinforcement without a clear developmental dependency—an awareness objective and an applied objective at the same grade with no evidence one is prerequisite to the other—so relatesTo (symmetric, null direction) is warranted over buildsTowards. Token overlap ('subtraction', 'pupils should be able to') alone would not suffice, but the shared everyday-subtraction concept does.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary Three Performance Objectives within the same Time topic (Mensuration and Geometry > Primary Measures). The first, 'mention the importance of time in daily life activities,' addresses the conceptual value/appreciation of time, while the second, 'say time accurately in hours and minutes,' is a procedural telling-time skill. They are complementary facets of the same time concept and share the LC tag 'time', giving substantive conceptual coherence. However, at the same grade rank (both PRIMARY THREE, rank gap 0) neither objective clearly depends on or develops from the other—appreciating the importance of time and reading the clock accurately are parallel aspects rather than a sequenced build. Shared row/page proximity and generic token overlap ('pupils should be able to', 'time') are context only, so relatesTo is warranted rather than a directional buildsTowards.

judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY ONE Performance Objectives under the same Sub-Theme 'Primary Measures' (Theme: Mensuration and Geometry). The first develops/demonstrates 'the idea of time' (Topic 3. Time); the second develops 'the idea of length' (Topic 2. Length). Both are foundational, parallel 'idea of' measurement concepts sharing the LC tags 'concept' and 'measurement', giving substantive conceptual coherence. This supports symmetric relatesTo rather than buildsTowards. The shared textual overlap is largely generic ('idea','of','the'), so the relation rests on genuine same-sub-theme measurement coherence, not wording alone.

judgment.rationale: Both are PRIMARY ONE Performance Objectives under the same Theme (NUMBER AND NUMERATION) and Sub-Theme (Whole Number), but sit in distinct Topics (Topic 4 'Whole number 10' vs Topic 2 'Whole number 0 (Zero)'). The first asks pupils to recognize 10 as a group; the second to recognize that the symbol 0 stands for nothingness. These are complementary early whole-number recognition skills that reinforce a shared number-sense strand, giving substantive conceptual coherence. The nomination overlap, however, is largely boilerplate ('pupil should be able to', 'recognize') and the shared LC token is the broad 'whole number'/'number' tag, so there is no evidence of a developmental dependency in either direction—both are same-rank (Grade PRIMARY ONE) foundational recognitions of different specific numbers. relatesTo (symmetric) fits better than a directional buildsTowards.
